themes: Theme
Core sub-themes
Illustrative quote
Meaning for operations
Fragmented recordkeeping creates no single source of truth
Manual and hybrid recording; person-dependent updates; informal workarounds.
"So far, we do not have a system for tracking our sales and inventory..." (Interviewee 1)
Operations depend on scattered records rather than a unified live record.
Delayed updates make the accurate picture arrive too late
Unposted movement; next-day correction; decisions made under uncertainty.
"The deeper issue is that the real situation becomes visible too late." (Interviewee 3)
Even when the truth is eventually reconstructed, it often arrives after the decision window.
Inaccurate records disrupt service, fulfillment, and restocking
Customer promise failure; partial release; conservative or delayed restocking.
"This can disappoint customers and reduce sales." (Interviewee 2)
Weak records quickly become visible as stockouts, delays, and missed sales.
Manual reconciliation shifts effort from operations to error correction
Repeated recounting; after-hours verification; coordination strain.
"Sometimes it ends up in an argument because I am already loaded with work." (Interviewee 1)
Labor is redirected from serving customers and planning toward repetitive correction.
When records conflict, trust shifts to physical proof
Physical count as truth; signed slips and receipts preferred; slow confirmation.
"We usually check the actual physical stock first because that is the most reliable basis." (Interviewee 2)
Record systems have not earned enough trust to support fast decisions on their own.
